title: Peculiar elongated and sickle-shaped red blood corpuscles in a case of severe anemia
citation: Herrick JB. Peculiar elongated and sickle-shaped red blood corpuscles in a case of severe anemia. Arch Intern Med. 1910;6(5):517-521.
established: First published description of sickled red cells, in a dental student from Grenada.
editorNote: Public domain. Free text is the 2001 Yale J Biol Med reprint (PMC2588723). Candidate for hosted download.

title: Sickle cell anemia, a molecular disease
citation: Pauling L, Itano HA, Singer SJ, Wells IC. Sickle cell anemia, a molecular disease. Science. 1949;110(2865):543-548.
established: Showed sickle hemoglobin differs physically from normal hemoglobin: the first disease traced to an abnormal protein.
editorNote: Scan at NLM Profiles in Science.

title: The inheritance of sickle cell anemia
citation: Neel JV. The inheritance of sickle cell anemia. Science. 1949;110(2846):64-66.
established: Established sickle cell anemia as a recessive trait: carriers have sickle cell trait, homozygotes have the disease.

title: Protection afforded by sickle-cell trait against subtertian malareal infection
citation: Allison AC. Protection afforded by sickle-cell trait against subtertian malareal infection. Br Med J. 1954;1(4857):290-294.
established: Explained why the sickle gene persists: carriers are protected against severe falciparum malaria.

title: Gene mutations in human haemoglobin: the chemical difference between normal and sickle cell haemoglobin
citation: Ingram VM. Gene mutations in human haemoglobin: the chemical difference between normal and sickle cell haemoglobin. Nature. 1957;180(4581):326-328.
established: Identified the cause as one amino acid change (glutamic acid to valine) in the beta-globin chain.
editorNote: Distinct from Ingram's 1956 Nature paper; 1957 is the one that names the substitution.

title: Prophylaxis with oral penicillin in children with sickle cell anemia. A randomized trial
citation: Gaston MH, Verter JI, Woods G, et al. Prophylaxis with oral penicillin in children with sickle cell anemia. A randomized trial. N Engl J Med. 1986;314(25):1593-1599.
established: Daily penicillin cut pneumococcal sepsis by 84% in young children; the trial was stopped early and led to universal prophylaxis and newborn screening.

title: Newborn screening for sickle cell disease: effect on mortality
citation: Vichinsky E, Hurst D, Earles A, Kleman K, Lubin B. Newborn screening for sickle cell disease: effect on mortality. Pediatrics. 1988;81(6):749-755.
established: Children diagnosed at birth and enrolled in comprehensive care had 1.8% mortality versus 8% for those diagnosed later.

title: Mortality in sickle cell disease. Life expectancy and risk factors for early death
citation: Platt OS, Brambilla DJ, Rosse WF, et al. Mortality in sickle cell disease. Life expectancy and risk factors for early death. N Engl J Med. 1994;330(23):1639-1644.
established: Median survival 42 years for men and 48 for women with sickle cell anemia; identified fetal hemoglobin as protective. Still the most cited survival figure.

title: Effect of hydroxyurea on the frequency of painful crises in sickle cell anemia
citation: Charache S, Terrin ML, Moore RD, et al. Effect of hydroxyurea on the frequency of painful crises in sickle cell anemia. N Engl J Med. 1995;332(20):1317-1322.
established: Hydroxyurea roughly halved painful crises, acute chest syndrome and transfusions in adults; the basis for the first FDA-approved sickle cell drug.

title: Bone marrow transplantation for sickle cell disease
citation: Walters MC, Patience M, Leisenring W, et al. Bone marrow transplantation for sickle cell disease. N Engl J Med. 1996;335(6):369-376.
established: First multicenter series showing matched-sibling transplant could cure children with severe disease.

title: Prevention of a first stroke by transfusions in children with sickle cell anemia and abnormal results on transcranial Doppler ultrasonography
citation: Adams RJ, McKie VC, Hsu L, et al. Prevention of a first stroke by transfusions in children with sickle cell anemia and abnormal results on transcranial Doppler ultrasonography. N Engl J Med. 1998;339(1):5-11.
established: Transcranial Doppler screening plus chronic transfusion cut first stroke by about 90%; stopped early for benefit.

title: Cerebrovascular accidents in sickle cell disease: rates and risk factors
citation: Ohene-Frempong K, Weiner SJ, Sleeper LA, et al. Cerebrovascular accidents in sickle cell disease: rates and risk factors. Blood. 1998;91(1):288-294.
established: Quantified stroke risk: about 11% of patients with sickle cell anemia have a stroke by age 20, highest in early childhood.
editorNote: Free on ashpublications.org. DOI not resolvable via Crossref; cite by PMID.

title: Causes and outcomes of the acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease
citation: Vichinsky EP, Neumayr LD, Earles AN, et al. Causes and outcomes of the acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease. National Acute Chest Syndrome Study Group. N Engl J Med. 2000;342(25):1855-1865.
established: Defined the causes (infection, fat embolism) and outcomes of acute chest syndrome and established early transfusion and bronchodilator care.

title: Effect of hydroxyurea on mortality and morbidity in adult sickle cell anemia: risks and benefits up to 9 years of treatment
citation: Steinberg MH, Barton F, Castro O, et al. Effect of hydroxyurea on mortality and morbidity in adult sickle cell anemia: risks and benefits up to 9 years of treatment. JAMA. 2003;289(13):1645-1651.
established: Nine-year follow-up of MSH: hydroxyurea use was associated with 40% lower mortality.

title: Human fetal hemoglobin expression is regulated by the developmental stage-specific repressor BCL11A
citation: Sankaran VG, Menne TF, Xu J, et al. Human fetal hemoglobin expression is regulated by the developmental stage-specific repressor BCL11A. Science. 2008;322(5909):1839-1842.
established: Identified BCL11A as the switch that silences fetal hemoglobin; the target of today's CRISPR therapy.
editorNote: No PMC version. PMC2854393 is a different Sankaran paper.

title: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for sickle cell disease
citation: Hsieh MM, Kang EM, Fitzhugh CD, et al. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for sickle cell disease. N Engl J Med. 2009;361(24):2309-2317.
established: Nonmyeloablative conditioning made transplant feasible for adults with organ damage, not just children.

title: Hydroxycarbamide in very young children with sickle-cell anaemia: a multicentre, randomised, controlled trial (BABY HUG)
citation: Wang WC, Ware RE, Miller ST, et al. Hydroxycarbamide in very young children with sickle-cell anaemia: a multicentre, randomised, controlled trial (BABY HUG). Lancet. 2011;377(9778):1663-1672.
established: Hydroxyurea was safe and reduced pain, dactylitis and hospitalisation in children aged 9 to 18 months; extended the drug to infancy.

title: Global epidemiology of sickle haemoglobin in neonates: a contemporary geostatistical model-based map and population estimates
citation: Piel FB, Patil AP, Howes RE, et al. Global epidemiology of sickle haemoglobin in neonates: a contemporary geostatistical model-based map and population estimates. Lancet. 2013;381(9861):142-151.
established: Estimated about 300,000 births with sickle cell anemia per year, three quarters in sub-Saharan Africa, with India the next largest burden.

title: Management of sickle cell disease: summary of the 2014 evidence-based report by expert panel members
citation: Yawn BP, Buchanan GR, Afenyi-Annan AN, et al. Management of sickle cell disease: summary of the 2014 evidence-based report by expert panel members. JAMA. 2014;312(10):1033-1048.
established: The reference guideline for day-to-day management: hydroxyurea for all with sickle cell anemia, TCD screening, pain management, transfusion indications.

title: Controlled trial of transfusions for silent cerebral infarcts in sickle cell anemia
citation: DeBaun MR, Gordon M, McKinstry RC, et al. Controlled trial of transfusions for silent cerebral infarcts in sickle cell anemia. N Engl J Med. 2014;371(8):699-710.
established: Chronic transfusion reduced recurrence of silent cerebral infarcts, the most common brain injury in children with the disease.

title: Reproductive issues in sickle cell disease
citation: Smith-Whitley K. Reproductive issues in sickle cell disease. Blood. 2014;124(24):3538-3543.
established: Framed fertility, contraception and pregnancy as part of routine sickle cell care as survival into adulthood became the norm.

title: Hydroxycarbamide versus chronic transfusion for maintenance of transcranial doppler flow velocities in children with sickle cell anaemia (TWiTCH)
citation: Ware RE, Davis BR, Schultz WH, et al. Hydroxycarbamide versus chronic transfusion for maintenance of transcranial doppler flow velocities in children with sickle cell anaemia (TWiTCH): a multicentre, open-label, phase 3, non-inferiority trial. Lancet. 2016;387(10019):661-670.
established: Hydroxyurea was non-inferior to transfusion for keeping TCD velocities down; offered a way off lifelong transfusion.

title: Gene therapy in a patient with sickle cell disease
citation: Ribeil JA, Hacein-Bey-Abina S, Payen E, et al. Gene therapy in a patient with sickle cell disease. N Engl J Med. 2017;376(9):848-855.
established: First report of lentiviral gene therapy (LentiGlobin) producing anti-sickling hemoglobin and resolving symptoms in a teenager.

title: A phase 3 trial of L-glutamine in sickle cell disease
citation: Niihara Y, Miller ST, Kanter J, et al. A phase 3 trial of L-glutamine in sickle cell disease. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(3):226-235.
established: L-glutamine reduced pain crises; the second FDA-approved drug for sickle cell disease, 19 years after hydroxyurea.

title: Hydroxyurea for children with sickle cell anemia in sub-Saharan Africa
citation: Tshilolo L, Tomlinson G, Williams TN, et al. Hydroxyurea for children with sickle cell anemia in sub-Saharan Africa. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(2):121-131.
established: Hydroxyurea was feasible, safe and effective in 606 children across Angola, DRC, Kenya and Uganda, with fewer malaria episodes and deaths.

title: Hydroxycarbamide exposure and ovarian reserve in women with sickle cell disease in the Multicenter Study of Hydroxycarbamide
citation: Pecker LH, Hussain S, Christianson MS, Lanzkron S. Hydroxycarbamide exposure and ovarian reserve in women with sickle cell disease in the Multicenter Study of Hydroxycarbamide. Br J Haematol. 2020;191(5):880-887.
established: Women with sickle cell anemia show diminished ovarian reserve from their mid-20s, and hydroxyurea exposure was independently associated with it; the evidence behind fertility-preservation counselling.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia
citation: Frangoul H, Altshuler D, Cappellini MD, et al. CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. N Engl J Med. 2021;384(3):252-260.
established: First patients treated with BCL11A-targeted CRISPR editing; both had sustained fetal hemoglobin and no vaso-occlusive events.

title: Biologic and clinical efficacy of LentiGlobin for sickle cell disease
citation: Kanter J, Walters MC, Krishnamurti L, et al. Biologic and clinical efficacy of LentiGlobin for sickle cell disease. N Engl J Med. 2022;386(7):617-628.
established: Pivotal data for lovotibeglogene autotemcel: complete resolution of severe vaso-occlusive events in treated patients; approved as Lyfgenia in December 2023.
editorNote: Title says LentiGlobin; the product is now lovo-cel / Lyfgenia.

title: Exagamglogene autotemcel for severe sickle cell disease
citation: Frangoul H, Locatelli F, Sharma A, et al. Exagamglogene autotemcel for severe sickle cell disease. N Engl J Med. 2024;390(18):1649-1662.
established: Pivotal trial of exa-cel: 97% of evaluable patients free of severe vaso-occlusive crises for at least 12 months; approved as Casgevy in December 2023.
